extracted.intended_audience: Researchers invited to review manuscripts for Nature Communications (peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers asked to review manuscripts for the multidisciplinary, open-access journal Nature Communications: deciding whether to accept, preparing and writing a constructive reviewer report, and using available training and recognition resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal scope and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, physical, chemical, Earth and social sciences. While Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals strive to publish the highest impact research within these disciplines, Nature Communications is committed to publishing important advances of significance to specialists within each field and multidisciplinary research across fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should judge whether a submission fits the journal's scope and whether it represents an important advance: evaluate its significance to specialists in the field and any multidisciplinary relevance or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before you accept
rubrics_metrics.description: What to consider before accepting an invitation to review a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page directs reviewers to consider key factors before accepting an invitation. While specifics are not listed on this page, reviewers should typically consider whether they have the appropriate subject-matter expertise, sufficient time to complete a careful review, and any potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read editorial policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you are new to reviewing for Nature Portfolio or experienced, please read our editorial policies before you begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected to be familiar with Nature Portfolio editorial policies prior to reviewing. These policies cover editorial/ethical standards and related requirements that may affect assessment and recommendations (see the journal's editorial policies pages for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing your report
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on how to assess a manuscript and write a useful reviewer report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should provide a useful, constructive report that assesses the manuscript's strengths and weaknesses, commenting on novelty/significance, experimental or methodological rigour, validity of results and interpretation, clarity of presentation, and providing actionable suggestions for improvement. Distinguish major issues that affect suitability for publication from minor points and editorial suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get recognition for your effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on the ways we recognise your reviewing activity for Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal provides mechanisms to acknowledge reviewer contributions; reviewers should consult the linked information to claim or record recognition (e.g., institutional or third-party services) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training
rubrics_metrics.description: For more training resources, see the free online course Focus on Peer Review from Nature Masterclasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature recommends that reviewers, especially early career researchers, make use of available training (such as the 'Focus on Peer Review' course) to learn best practices in evaluating manuscripts and writing reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review initiatives and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Our initiatives to improve the quality and transparency of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware of and comply with the journal's initiatives aimed at improving peer review quality and transparency. Specific initiatives and expectations are detailed on the linked pages (e.g., policies around openness, recognition, and review processes).
